root_idea.summary: The root centers on شَيْخ, a person advanced in age. Age is associated in the lexical tradition with accumulated experience, knowledge, and social precedence.
root_idea.development: The family develops from becoming old and the state of old age to honorific titles and several figurative or specialized applications; derived verbal forms include calling someone a shaykh, imputing faults, and feigning old age.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular citation form شَيْخ; the QAC group includes its plural شُيُوخ.

senses.definition: A person advanced in age; an old or elderly man.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage it describes advanced age, in both singular and plural forms, including an old husband or father and old men. The lexical range can include an elder who retains strength as well as one who is weak or decrepit; weakness and honorific status are not required by the word itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become old or elderly; to reach the condition of a shaykh.
To call someone a shaykh as an act of honor or respect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative or honorific naming use of the Form II verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To attribute or charge someone with a vice or fault; to blame or reproach him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Explicitly associated with the construction شَيَّخَ عَلَيْهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To expose someone’s vices or evil actions; to disgrace or put him to shame.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Associated with the construction شَيَّخَ بِهِ and related usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feign or make a show of old age.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form V usage distinct from actually growing old.
The feminine counterpart of شَيْخ in its age-related sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An honorific title for a learned man, especially a doctor of religion or law; also a religious leader, tribal or village chief, or reputed saint.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later or customary honorific application, distinct from the literal description of age.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An honorific title for a learned woman, instructress, or the like.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later or customary feminine honorific application.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A title specifically applied to Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed honorific title for the two early caliphs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman’s husband, even when he is young.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or transferred usage in which the word does not require the husband to be old.
A figurative usage, attested in expressions referring to one’s forefathers or ancestors.
A fixed figurative expression, explained by his creation from fire or his ultimate abode in Hellfire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An aged or full-grown mountain goat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transferred animal-designation based on advanced age or maturity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The roots or fixed bases of the stars; in traditional astronomical interpretation, the expression may refer to seven or five planets or to fixed stars outside the lunar mansions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized astronomical expression with variant traditional identifications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain tree whose fruit resembles that of the bastard saffron.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct botanical noun, also called شَجَرَةُ الشُّيُوخِ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Form I verb meaning: to become a shaykh or grow old.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the preceding paragraph.
Honorific naming use of Form II.
Two distinct fault-imputation and fault-exposure constructions.
Form V meaning: to feign old age.
Core age-related meaning, feminine counterpart, and male and female honorific extensions.
Fixed title for Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
Animal designation for an aged or full-grown mountain goat.
Feminine-form cross-reference; it adds no meaning beyond the feminine branch already stated under شَيْخ.
Diminutive-form listing without an independent lexical meaning.

cautions: The single QAC form group combines singular شَيْخ and plural شُيُوخ under the normalized citation headword شَيْخ.
The astronomical expression أَشْيَاخُ النُّجُومِ has variant traditional interpretations.
